Under ADR-045 (still a draft), a re:cinq npm package is published by a GitHub Actions release workflow. It runs on `push` of tags matching `v*`, and can also be started with `workflow_dispatch`. The workflow has `permissions: contents: read` plus `id-token: write`. It installs `npm@^11.5.1` globally, because OIDC trusted publishing needs that version or newer and Node 22 ships an older npm. It then runs `npm publish --provenance --access public`. Auth is npm Trusted Publishing over OIDC. A trusted publisher is registered on npmjs.com for the package, pointing at the repo and workflow, so no `NPM_TOKEN` secret is used. The exception is the very first publish of a new package name. That is done once with a short-lived token, because the trusted publisher can only be registered after the package exists. The token is then revoked. A private-source repo such as bowman-ui omits `--provenance`, since provenance needs a public source repo. New workflows must also use `persist-credentials: false`, `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, job-scoped token permissions, and third-party actions pinned by commit SHA. The package manifest must be under the `@re-cinq` scope, with Apache-2.0 licence, ESM, `files: [dist]`, an `exports` map, and `publishConfig.access: public`.

The release job first compares the git tag with the committed `package.json` version and fails before publishing if they disagree. This is a guard against a past failure. Tags `v0.5.0` through `v0.7.0` published nothing, and npm stayed on `0.3.0` for nine weeks. npm rejects a duplicate version in a way that looks like an auth failure, so nobody investigated. The guard turns that silent failure into a red CI job that names the fix. The reference implementation is `ai-agent-subsystem/scripts/check-contracts-version.sh` (ai-agent-subsystem#139). An October 2026 amendment adds that the changelog heading change, `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] - date`, goes in the same commit as the `package.json` bump the guard compares against the tag.

judgements.reason: The answer covers the v* tag workflow, npm publish --provenance via OIDC Trusted Publishing without NPM_TOKEN (first-publish short-lived token exception), and the tag/package.json guard motivated by v0.5.0–v0.7.0 publishing nothing for nine weeks due to duplicate-version rejection resembling an auth failure.
